messages:
maria: Heads-up — support forwarded a contract request from a large fintech. They're asking for a formal commitment: 99.95% uptime + latency SLO for production text-gen routes. Ticket attached.
emily (CSM): Customer name: HarborFin. They've been hitting lat spikes during market opens. Asking for P95 <= 250ms for short chat queries and a 4hr incident SLA. Want to know if we can commit on Dedicated or need Private.
tom (sales): They're asking this as part of a renewal conversation. Renewal talk starts next month — sales needs a clear yes/no and rough timeline. If we need Dedicated it's fine, they'll pay for reserved capacity.
devon: Quick triage: what route(s) exactly? chat vs batch embeddings vs streaming? We need to scope. Also need expected qps and burst profile. Can CSM share traces?
emily (CSM): Shared traces in the ticket. Peak bursts ~120 qps for short messages (<=128 tokens) during 30m windows. Normal baseline ~15 qps.
sanjay: From runtime: for that qps on current model we see P95 ~310ms on hosted multi-tenant. With Dedicated and some batching/caching we can get to ~180–220ms. Achieving <=250ms P95 is realistic on Dedicated with a config change.
maria: Good. Ask legal: do we want to add this as an SLA or a contractual appendix? Also, what penalty/credits language will we accept?
deploy-bot: new file uploaded: `harborfin-traces-2026-03-15.zip`
tom (sales): Legal will push for narrow wording: uptime for API endpoint + failure modes (control plane vs data plane). We should outline fallback behavior: auto-fallback to a lower-cost model or degraded SLA.
devon: Proposal for intake -> routing: 1) classify as Contract-SLO request. 2) Create product backlog epic with tags [contract-slo, enterprise, dedicated]. 3) Run quick feasibility with Eng (2-day spike). 4) Draft appendix for Legal. 5) Sales/CSM coordinate pricing for Dedicated commit. Can we accept that flow?
maria: Yes. I'll create the epic and own the spike. Can Eng produce a small matrix of options: Hosted (no commit) vs Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) vs Private (on-prem/VPC) with expected P95 numbers, cost delta, and rollout risk.
sanjay: I'll do the spike. Deliverables: perf matrix, deployment plan (canary + automatic fallback), and regression test plan (synthetic traffic). ETA 3 business days.
emily (CSM): I'll gather exact SLA language they've seen elsewhere and push the traces & SLO target to the ticket.
maria: For prioritization: label as P1 contract intake. If spike shows feasible on Dedicated within 3 weeks, we aim for a canary rollout in the next monthly release. If not, we offer a fallback (higher latency SLO or dedicated-only solution).
tom (sales): I'll tell the customer we're running a technical spike and will confirm feasibility in 3 business days. Thanks.
sanjay: One more note — if they require geo-redundant uptime (99.99+) we'll need multi-region Dedicated or Private with cross-region failover. That shifts cost and timeline significantly.
maria: Noted. Adding that as a conditional in the epic. Action items: (maria) create epic + intake form link; (sanjay) perf spike; (emily) finalize traces and customer SLO doc; (tom) update customer. I'll ping legal after spike.
emily (CSM): :thumbsup: Will do.
maria: Closing loop here — will post spike results in this thread when ready.
